body:
## Summary

If `copy-to-skill-dirs.sh` is invoked with an empty string `""` or `.` as a target directory argument (e.g. from an unset or empty shell variable, or user input), `destination` resolves to the project root directory itself.

The script only guards against `destination == canonical_skills_dir` (`.agents/skills`), not against `destination == project_root`. Consequently, it treats the project root as a skill directory, deletes any root files or directories whose names match managed skills (`rm -rf "${destination:?}/${name}"`), writes `.sync-jonbaldie-skills.manifest` directly into the project root, and copies skills into the root directory.

## Reproduction

```bash
bash - <<'BASH'
set -euo pipefail
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${TMP}"' EXIT

mkdir -p "${TMP}/project/.agents/skills/alpha"
echo "valuable project file" > "${TMP}/project/alpha"
echo "---" > "${TMP}/project/.agents/skills/alpha/SKILL.md"
echo "name: alpha" >> "${TMP}/project/.agents/skills/alpha/SKILL.md"
echo "---" >> "${TMP}/project/.agents/skills/alpha/SKILL.md"
printf "alpha\n" > "${TMP}/project/.agents/sync-jonbaldie-skills.manifest"

skills/sync-jonbaldie-skills/scripts/copy-to-skill-dirs.sh "${TMP}/project" ""
cat "${TMP}/project/alpha/SKILL.md"
BASH
```

Observed output:
```text
  copied alpha -> /tmp/.../project
Additional destination: /tmp/.../project
---
name: alpha
---
```
The file `${TMP}/project/alpha` was removed and replaced by directory `alpha/` containing `SKILL.md`.

## Expected behavior

`copy-to-skill-dirs.sh` should validate that each target directory argument is non-empty and does not resolve to the project root (`${destination} == ${project_root}`), rejecting such arguments with an error before performing any operations.

## Evidence

- `skills/sync-jonbaldie-skills/scripts/copy-to-skill-dirs.sh:35-54`:
  ```bash
  copy_to_directory() {
    local requested_directory="$1"
    local destination
    local destination_manifest
    local name

    if [[ "${requested_directory}" = /* ]]; then
      destination="${requested_directory}"
    else
      destination="${project_root}/${requested_directory}"
    fi

    mkdir -p "${destination}"
    destination="$(cd "${destination}" && pwd -P)"

    if [[ "${destination}" == "${canonical_skills_dir}" ]]; then
      printf 'Already canonical: %s\n' "${destination}"
      return
    fi
  ```
  When `requested_directory` is `""` or `.`, `destination` resolves to `${project_root}`. Because `${project_root}` is not equal to `${canonical_skills_dir}` (`.agents/skills`), it proceeds to delete matching entries in `${project_root}` and install skills there.
